metadata.title: Isaiah Bond Lacks Consistent Role
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Isaiah Bond hasn't seen much of the field during the first two games of the regular season. He wasn't targeted at all in the season opener, and Bond only saw one target during the win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last week. The 22-year-old is barely getting on the field right now, as he played only seven percent of the offensive snaps last week. It's tough to imagine Bond getting a larger role in the passing attack unless someone ahead of him gets injured. Bond showed some promising flashes during his rookie season, but is unlikely to be a big contributor in 2026. Given he's only 22 years old, Bond has some dynasty stash value, but he's not someone who is likely going to contribute much right now.

metadata.title: Isaiah Bond (concussion) back at practice Monday
metadata.description: Isaiah Bond returned to practice on Monday.
metadata.analysis: Bond missed some recent practice time with a concussion. He remains off the fantasy radar heading into the season.

metadata.title: Isaiah Bond - Past concussion issue
metadata.description: Bond (concussion) has cleared protocol and is practicing Monday, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
metadata.analysis: Bond was concussed in Cleveland's second preseason game and was nearing 100 percent at the end of August. He's expected to fill the WR4 role for the Browns behind KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston and veteran Jerry Jeudy. As a rookie last season, Bond caught just 18 of 44 targets for 338 yards and zero touchdowns as a deep threat.

metadata.title: Isaiah Bond (concussion) misses practice
metadata.description: Isaiah Bond did not practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Bond had reportedly cleared concussion protocol, so it is unclear what happened. His status for Week 1 is up in the air.

metadata.title: Isaiah Bond clears concussion protocol
metadata.description: Browns WR Isaiah Bond cleared concussion protocol.
metadata.analysis: Bond is competing for a depth role in the Browns wide receiver room.

metadata.title: Isaiah Bond - Absent from practice Monday
metadata.description: Bond (concussion) is not practicing Monday, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
metadata.analysis: Bond continues to deal with the concussion he sustained in Cleveland's second preseason game, but coach Todd Monken said Monday the wideout is nearing a return to the field. Bond is expected to open the season as a sub-package wide receiver behind Jerry Jeudy and rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston while also handling returner duties. Bond doesn't carry much fantasy value outside of return yardage leagues.

metadata.title: Isaiah Bond - Clears concussion protocol
metadata.description: Bond cleared concussion protocol during Saturday's preseason game against the Bills.
metadata.analysis: Bond was flagged to be evaluated for a possible concussion during the second quarter of Saturday's exhibition contest. He's been cleared to return to the game, but it remains to be seen whether he'll see the field over the last two quarters.

metadata.title: Isaiah Bond - Getting checked for possible concussion
metadata.description: Bond is being evaluated for a possible concussion and is questionable to return to Saturday's preseason game against the Bills.
metadata.analysis: Bond was flagged by one of the concussion spotters during the second quarter of Saturday's exhibition game, and he has been taken to the locker room to undergo further tests. Assuming his day is done, Bond will finish with one catch on as many targets for eight yards along with a four-yard carry.

metadata.title: Isaiah Bond Has a Lot to Prove in Preseason Action
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Isaiah Bond is highlighted by Zac Jackson of The Athletic as one of Cleveland's players with the most to prove in the team's upcoming preseason game against the Buffalo Bills. Bond flashed upside but also battled inconsistency as a rookie in 2025, recording 18 catches for 338 yards on 44 targets across 16 games (two starts). However, the Browns added significant talent to their wide receiver room over the offseason by using top-40 selections in the 2026 NFL Draft on wideouts KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston. Veteran wide receivers Jerry Jeudy and Cedric Tillman remain potential factors in Cleveland as well. While the 22-year-old Bond still offers some potential, it appears as though he may need to show well in the Browns' remaining preseason games to assure his place in the team's plans for 2026.

metadata.title: Isaiah Bond Needs a Big Camp to Keep Dynasty Appeal
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Isaiah Bond flashed enough as a rookie to stay on the dynasty radar, but the roster got a lot less forgiving this spring. He turned 44 targets into 18 catches for 338 yards, an 18.8-yard average, without finding the end zone. Cleveland then used the 24th and 39th picks on KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston. Jerry Jeudy and Cedric Tillman are still here, too. Bond did help himself during offseason work. He added roughly 15 pounds, looked stronger through contact, and made plays at every level of the field. The Browns praised the progress, though none of it guarantees him a regular role once camp begins. Cleveland also has an unsettled quarterback competition, which does not help a receiver fighting for the back end of the rotation. RotoBaller has Bond 269th overall in its latest dynasty rankings. That is deep-league territory. He is worth tracking through August, not forcing onto ordinary dynasty rosters before the depth chart starts to clear.

metadata.title: Isaiah Bond - Strong spring
metadata.description: Bond added 15 pounds of muscle during the offseason and was one of the Browns' standout performers during spring practices, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: According to Oyefusi, Bond led the team in targets during spring practices and "continued to display his speed" while also making "a bunch of contested catches." Cleveland used early draft picks on wide receivers KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston back in April, and the team also still employs Jerry Jeudy (hamstring) and Cedric Tillman, so it's unclear how this wideout depth chart is going to shake out over the summer. Bond is putting himself in the mix after securing just 18 of 44 targets for 338 yards and no touchdowns across 16 regular-season games as a rookie last season.
